messages.text: Take {gift_item}. Better to carry thanks before you need steel.
Here, {gift_item}. I trust you to use it with a cooler head than most.
Then the advice kept its edge. {tested_villager} liked {gift_item}.
That blade was poorly balanced. For {gift_subject}, try {alternative_gift}.
{gift_item} missed clean? Bring {alternative_gift}; better weight for the hand.

openings.text: Mind the grindstone. What do you need?

closings.text: Back to keeping blades honest, then.

lines.text: Rust on a sword is just neglect learning to speak.
Trouble always finds villages. Best be ready.
The golem did good work last night. Still, I keep the blades sharp.
Mind the grindstone. It has no patience for wandering fingers.
A blade tells the truth about its owner sooner or later.
Ready is not the same as eager. A village should know the difference.
I once polished rust off a sword and found three old mistakes underneath.
Weapon jokes are sharp. I keep the dull ones for people who lean too close.
That was dull enough to be safe, at least.
Keeping an edge honest is mostly knowing when to stop grinding.
An unready guard is just confidence standing in the wrong place.
Some nights, the grindstone sounds like preparation instead of work.
Stand back. I know the sound trouble makes when it wants to be casual.

pacify.text: Fine. I will let the blade rest, but do not test me again.
No. Some threats do not get to buy their way closer.
